page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6t.13xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance belonging to the Enhanced ecs.c6t family. Built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via a KVM hypervisor, this instance features 52 dedicated vCPUs driven by Intel Xeon 8269CY processors running at a base clock frequency of 2.5 GHz. System memory is provisioned at 96.0 GB total, establishing a lean memory allocation ratio of 1.85 GB per vCPU core designed specifically for processing-heavy workloads.

The hardware configuration contains no discrete GPUs and relies entirely on external network-attached storage, as zero local SSD or HDD storage is bundled with the instance. Network connectivity is supported by a 16 Gbps baseline bandwidth interface, facilitating consistent data transmission between compute nodes and remote storage volumes.

With a high core count relative to its memory footprint, the instance offers strong cost efficiency for multithreaded compute tasks that do not demand large per-core memory capacity. Tradeoffs include the requirement for external storage management and potential memory throttling under high-capacity RAM demands. Recommended workload fits include CPU-bound batch processing, compilation systems, distributed microservices, and general compute-heavy parallel tasks.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6t.13xlarge is a compute-optimized instance within the Enhanced family. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at 2.5 GHz, it provides 52 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs running on a KVM hypervisor. The instance is configured with 96.0 GB of system memory, yielding a compute-dense ratio of approximately 1.85 GB per vCPU. It features no local disk storage, relying on external network-attached block storage, and includes no discrete GPU hardware. Network capabilities include a 16 Gbps baseline bandwidth. This instance profile delivers qualitative cost efficiency for highly parallel CPU-bound computational workloads that do not require massive per-core memory allocation, such as batch data processing, distributed compute tasks, software build nodes, and compute-heavy microservice architectures.
